0.badge: 1 • WELCOMING THE MOMENT • PASSING IT ON

1.title: The symbolic handover
1.subtitle: Passing on. Recognising. Letting you live your own life.

p.1:
It’s a big day for you…

But for me, it’s an important moment too.
p.2:
For years I have been gathering, in my own way, memories, moments, traces of your path.

Simple moments, sometimes quiet ones, but which, for me, tell something precious: the story we have shared.
p.3:
This Carnet is a trace of that bond.

A living memory of what I saw, felt and understood as I watched you grow.
p.4:
It is not a truth about you.

It is how I saw things, in my words, with my story and my limits.

I did my best with who I am.
p.5:
Today, I pass it on to you as a gesture of love across the years.

Perhaps it will help you understand where you come from, what you have been through and who was around you.
p.6:
But this Carnet does not define you.

You remain free to become who you wish to be.

1.quote: Receiving your story means being able to connect with it while staying free to write what comes next.

2.label: Handing on
2.title: Handing on
2.intro:
This story was written over time.

It was made of presence, of bonds, of shared moments.

What I saw, felt and wished to pass on… is now part of this path.



Today, this Carnet passes from my hands to yours.

You can read it now, later, all at once or in pieces.

Come back to it.

Step away from it.

See it differently as time goes by.



What you do with it is yours.

And perhaps the most beautiful handing-on will be the one you choose to transform, or to create in your turn.

5.quote: Everyone passes things on in their own way, with their words… or with silence.

p.1:
I haven’t said everything in this Carnet.

And perhaps I haven’t always known how to say things, either.

But if I were to leave you a few words today, they would be these.
p.2:
I watched you grow.

In your own way.

With your strengths, your doubts, your drive.
p.3:
I saw some things change in you.

Others stay.
p.4:
Sometimes I understood.

Sometimes not so much.
p.5: I have certainly made mistakes, and there are things I would do differently today.
p.6:
But this Carnet was never meant to tell you who you should become.

It simply tells part of your story as I lived it alongside you.
p.7: I hope it can help you find forgotten moments, voices, faces, emotions, pieces of your childhood and your teenage years.
p.8:
You may recognise some things in it.

Discover others.

Disagree with some.

And perhaps see them differently as time goes by.
p.9:
What I wanted to pass on to you here is not a model to follow.

It is a trace.

A trace of what I saw.

Of what I felt.

Of what I tried to understand.

And above all, of the bond that has joined us all these years.
p.10:
What comes next doesn’t belong to me.

It is yours.
